court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: In an executors' accounting proceeding, the court found valid inter vivos gifts of mortgages and, separately, of Liberty bonds that the decedent had given to the landlady with whom he rented rooms and boarded for fourteen years, based on the decedent's admissions and surrounding circumstances.

quotes.text: The objections relate chiefly to four gifts, two to George F. Wiemann, one of the executors, a third to his brother, Albert B. Wiemann, and a fourth to one Clara Pallehner from whom decedent rented rooms and with whom he boarded for fourteen years.
He died at a rooming house conducted by Clara Pallehner, with whom he had resided for fourteen years.
The testator intended to give and did give these bonds to Clara Pallehner.

notes: Boarding relationship (rooms rented, board provided, personal care given) is background/incidental to a gift-law dispute, not itself litigated; the court never characterizes its legality, so polarity/characterization here reflect the case's neutral, unremarkable treatment of a long-running lodger relationship rather than a holding on point. Duration (14 years) and scale (single boarder vs. enterprise) do not fit the fixed categories, hence 'unclear' for both.
